candidate.title: 2b-RAD
candidate.scope: The 2b-RAD row of the assigned Illumina poster crop, interpreted as the standard BsaXI example with compatible NNN-ended adapters described in Wang et al. (2012), including its Illumina library interface. BsaXI is shown as an example of type IIB enzymes, not as a claim that all 2b-RAD implementations use this enzyme. The neighboring PE RAD-Seq, ddRADseq, SLAF-seq and partial cytosine-conversion panel are outside this card. The row has one route, with no depicted branching or pooling; repeated fragment lines are schematic examples, not separately routed sample branches. The paper-supported final barcode PCR covers both adjacent captions Add sample-specific adapters and Amplify. The depicted endpoint is DNA library, not sequencing data.

evidence.locator: Heading and introductory paragraph, BsaXI tag length
evidence.quote:
2b-RAD: RAD With Type IIB Restriction Endonucleases
2b-RAD is similar to ddRadseq but uses type IIB restriction enzymes (BsaXI or AlfI), which will cleave upstream and downstream of
a recognition site. This shears the target genome into a large number of DNA fragments with a constant length of 33 bp (BsaXI) or
36 bp (AlfI). These short DNA fragments can be sequenced to determine genetic variants.
evidence.rationale: This verified catalogue heading matches the assigned 2b-RAD row. Only its BsaXI description is used for the depicted example; the textual AlfI alternative does not create an additional drawn route.

states.label: Final sample-barcoded DNA library
features: PCR copies of genomic restriction tags carrying adapter-derived sequencing interfaces and sample-specific barcodes.
The colored terminal extensions denote sample-specific adapter information; the final DNA icon simplifies these features to blue lines.

Sequencing these DNA inserts and their associated sample identifiers supports variant discovery and genotyping at represented, distinguishable loci. The library samples restriction-site-defined genomic regions; short tags can limit locus discrimination in complex genomes.

operations.label: Restriction digestion with type IIB restriction endonucleases e.g. BsaXI
operations.description: Genomic DNA is cleaved on both sides of type IIB recognition sites, producing short, uniform-length site-associated genomic tags.

operations.information_effect: Retains short genomic segments associated with type IIB recognition sites, reducing the represented genome to a restriction-site-defined set of tags rather than an exhaustive genome sequence.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and labeled 2b-RAD row identify one target method. The BsaXI example resolves to the standard NNN-compatible adapter workflow described in the original paper, whose Online Methods distinguish an Illumina primer interface. The row accounts for digestion, restriction-adapter ligation, first amplification, and sample-specific adapter/barcode addition with final amplification. AlfI and selective-overhang preparations discussed in the papers are unshown implementations and do not add branches. Although the secondary catalogue prose mentions combining samples after adapter ligation, this row draws no pooling operation and the primary paper describes initial PCR per sample; no pre-barcode sample-mixing route is asserted.

corrections.diagram_observation: The poster labels Add sample-specific adapters beside colored terminal extensions, followed by a separate Amplify caption. It does not identify the chemistry of barcode attachment.

The final two captions are therefore represented together as barcode PCR, preserving the drawn order after initial amplification and avoiding an unsupported second ligation.

checks.rationale: The correction is supported for the declared standard BsaXI/Illumina implementation. The poster separately prints Add sample-specific adapters and Amplify without specifying a second attachment chemistry; the primary paper explicitly introduces barcodes by a final PCR using platform-specific primers. o4 preserves both captions and their position after initial amplification while identifying their common molecular transformation. This combines barcode incorporation and copying in one PCR, with one input and output; it does not combine independently routed samples or invent a second ligation. The distinction between the poster observation and primary-paper interpretation remains explicit.
